scholarships.title: Helmut Veith Stipend for Female Master's Students in Computer Science

existing.description: The Helmut Veith Stipend is an annually awarded grant for women pursuing a Master's programme in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English, created in memory of Professor Helmut Veith (1971-2016). TU Wien states the benefits as "EUR 7000 per year" plus a "Waiver of tuition fees at TU Wien". The fund is set up by TU Wien, the Wolfgang Pauli Institute and the colleagues and friends of the late Prof. Veith. Applications are submitted electronically through the TU Wien job portal and are due by 30 November each year.
eligibility: Female students in the field of computer science (CS)
(Plan to) pursue one of the Master's programmes in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English
Eligible for admission to one of the English-taught Master's programmes in Computer Science at TU Wien
Have, or have the interest to develop, a solid mathematical and technical background in at least one of the areas in which Austrian scientist Helmut Veith worked
Unconditionally admitted to the Master's programme at the time funding is awarded
existing.eligibility_summary: Women applying to or already admitted to an English-taught Master's programme in Computer Science at TU Wien, with a solid mathematical and technical background in at least one area in which Helmut Veith worked.
benefits: Waiver of tuition fees at TU Wien
coverage: Cash stipend of EUR 7,000 per year
Waiver of tuition fees at TU Wien
requirements: Applications for funding may be filed before or in parallel with the admissions process, but funding is only awarded to applicants who have been unconditionally admitted to the Master's programme
An application for funding does not replace the admissions process, and a conditional offer of funding does not entitle the applicant to study at TU Wien
existing.english_requirement: The Master's programme applied for must be one of the Computer Science Master's programmes at TU Wien that are taught in English.
application_method: Submit the application electronically via the TU Wien job portal
existing.best_fit: Women entering or continuing an English-taught CS Master's at TU Wien with a background in logic, formal methods and verification, artificial intelligence, algorithms and complexity, or computer security.
existing.notes: The eight English-taught CS Master's programmes currently listed by TU Wien are: Data Science; Business Informatics; Logic and Artificial Intelligence; Media and Human-Centered Computing; Software Engineering; Quantum Information Science and Technology; Embedded Computing Systems; Visual Computing.
existing.application_period: Applications are invited from November and close annually on 30 November.
existing.program_type: Merit-based scholarship for female computer science master's students

scholarships.title: Mannagetta Fellowships (Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation at the Austrian Academy of Sciences)
scholarships.official_source: Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation (Austrian Academy of Sciences)

existing.description: The Mannagetta Fellowships are financed from the funds of the Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation held at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and support doctoral candidates at Austrian universities in completing a doctoral thesis in the humanities, cultural and social sciences. Applicants must have started their doctoral studies at a university in Austria no more than three years before the submission deadline and need no more than another twelve months to finish. Each fellowship is worth EUR 25,000 for twelve months, and one or two fellowships are granted per year. Applications for the next round close on 20 October 2026 at 2 p.m. CEST.
eligibility: Young, highly qualified doctoral candidates pursuing doctoral studies at a university in Austria
Doctoral or PhD studies started no more than three years before the submission deadline
Expected to need no more than another twelve months to complete the doctoral thesis
Dissertation project in one of the listed subject areas
existing.eligibility_summary: Young, highly qualified doctoral candidates enrolled at a university in Austria who started their doctoral studies no more than three years before the submission deadline and expect to need no more than a further twelve months to complete the thesis.
benefits: EUR 25,000 stipend for a twelve-month fellowship period
coverage: Cash stipend of EUR 25,000 intended to contribute to covering living expenses
No travel or printing allowances: the statutes state these cannot be applied for
requirements: The programme statutes of the Mannagetta Fellowships and the guidelines for good scientific practice must be observed
Signing the online application form confirms that the applicant wrote the project proposal independently

Exceptions to the three-year rule are possible on proof of care responsibilities, illness or disability, but must be clarified with the OeAW Department of Fellowships and Awards before the application is submitted
Other funding applications may be made, but they and their outcome must be reported in writing to the Department of Fellowships and Awards
documents: Online application form for the Mannagetta Fellowship Program

Detailed description of the dissertation project of 10 to 15 pages, including theoretical foundations and research question(s), previous preliminary work, and a detailed time and work plan for the requested funding period
Application documents submitted through the OeAW online application form
application_method: Online application via the OeAW online application form for the Mannagetta Fellowship Program
existing.selection_notes: One or two fellowships can be granted per year. The awarding is handled by a selection committee and ultimately decided by the board of trustees of the Mannagetta Foundation.
existing.best_fit: Doctoral candidates in the final stage of a humanities, law, art history or archaeology dissertation at an Austrian university, who started their doctorate within the last three years.
existing.notes: The fellowship must be started within three months of notification of the award, and a copy of the completed dissertation together with proof of submission for review must be supplied no later than three months after the end of the funding period. Publications resulting from the funding must carry the note "funded within the Mannagetta Fellowship Program of the OeAW". There is no entitlement to the award and legal recourse is excluded.
existing.application_period: Applications for the 2026 round close on 20 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST; the fellowship is awarded once or twice per year.
existing.program_type: Completion fellowship for doctoral candidates in the humanities, social sciences, law and arts disciplines
